title: Zoom in on one named detail
subtitle: Rhetorical Synthesis · 51 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **51 of the official questions in Rhetorical Synthesis are this one** — 19 Easy, 30 Medium, 2 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:

- The goal names one specific thing: a single work, one year, one feature, one aspect (for example 'describe the setting of X', 'describe how material is used in Y', 'accomplishments before event Z').
- The notes cover several related things, and the answer choices are all accurate sentences drawn from different parts of the notes.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Underline the exact noun and restriction in the goal (which item, which time period, which feature).
- 2) Cross out any choice that is mainly about a different item or time, or about the general topic.
- 3) Pick the choice whose main clause directly gives that detail.
- The target has to be the subject of the sentence, not tucked into a side clause.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: Every choice is true to the notes, so if you check for accuracy you'll keep all four.
The trap choices mention the right name but describe the wrong thing, such as the author's biography instead of the novel's setting, or a later period when the goal says 'before'.
Some cover the whole collection when the goal asks about one member of it.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
